deadlineRule.rule: streamingReadMs(bytes) = readMs (10 min) x max(1, ceil(bytes / 128 MiB))
deadlineRule.appliesTo: the streaming-vector worker's whole-object read (openObjectStream timeout)
deadlineRule.notScaled: chunk-mapping and streamed-profile waits are per published chunk and reset after each one

readerSpeedFix.finding: the reader awaited a promise for every byte of every feature; on this PC the base reader took 212.96 s for the 43,263,076-byte NYC file (about 0.2 MB/s), so even a 128 MiB file would pass its 10-minute deadline and 1 GiB would need about 85 minutes before any database work
readerSpeedFix.change: Cursor.value takes a byte already in the current chunk without a wait; only an exhausted chunk awaits the next one. Offsets, hash, bounds and error codes are unchanged

realInputs.note: measured while the backend suite ran; the 435 set-aside numbers are the reader's existing rule

readerSpeedFix.measuredWith: reader + sourceRecord + part writer + encodeChunk, no database, no object storage (a scratch harness, not committed)

memoryProof.input: test_only FeatureCollection of 500,000 closed squares generated as a stream inside the test; never written to disk
memoryProof.reading: after collection the heap is flat from the first 500 parts to the last; the peak is collector headroom, reached already in the first tenth of the run (first run: 364.5 MiB in the first tenth, 368.3 MiB overall, with the base reader's per-byte waits)
